title: 清明
author: Du Mu

translation: During the Qingming festival, the rain falls in endless threads
Travelers on the road seem ready to break with sorrow
I ask where a tavern might be found
A shepherd boy points to the distant Apricot Blossom Village

annotations.清明: Qingming Festival — the day Chinese families sweep ancestral tombs
annotations.纷纷: falling thick and fast — describing the drizzling rain
annotations.借问: may I ask — a polite way to inquire

appreciation: The most famous poem about the Qingming Festival, when families honor their ancestors. The drizzling rain mirrors the mourners' mood. But the poem ends on a gentle turn: a shepherd boy points toward a village of apricot blossoms and wine, offering warmth amid sorrow.
